name: Reactive scheduler
description: Test correlated event dispatch, race selection, cancellation, stalled-work detection, reassignment, and teardown.

variants.description: Drive a ten-task queue through three deterministic workers with replayable events and controlled delay/failure patterns.
setup: Create a run-scoped event cursor and queue ledger before launching three deterministic workers.
Configure workers to emit correlated completions, one duplicate event, one delayed task, and one recoverable failure.
exercise: Dispatch only after the listener is active, consume completion events, ignore duplicates, and hand the next queued task to the freed worker.
Race three workers for one task, accept the first valid artifact, cancel synthetic losers, detect a stalled task by deadline plus no-progress evidence, reassign it, and drain the queue.

assertions.expectation: The event listener and cursor exist before the first task dispatch.
Every queue task reaches terminal state exactly once despite a replayed duplicate event.
The winner is the first valid correlated artifact, not merely the first unrelated or malformed event.
Reassignment uses deadline and progress evidence; CPU usage is recorded only as telemetry.
The queue, cursor, workers, surfaces, and workspace are fully reclaimed.

cleanup: Signal all synthetic workers, close only owned surfaces, and stop the event consumer at the run terminal state.
Delete the queue and cursor fixtures after recording their final hashes.

variants.description: Run a bounded read-only race and cancellation flow with real agents and run-scoped notifications.
setup: Create a secret-free disposable repo, three run-owned agent surfaces, and a listener filtered to the exact run workspace and surface IDs.
Define a read-only task, valid artifact schema, bounded deadline, and graceful cancellation deadline.
exercise: Dispatch the same correlated task to all agents, accept the first valid result event, and notify only with the run ID and non-sensitive status.
Request graceful stop from losing agents and close only their owned surfaces if the deadline expires.

assertions.expectation: Unrelated notification and agent events are ignored and never cause focus or cancellation.
The selected winner has a valid run nonce, request ID, schema, and evidence; arrival time alone is insufficient.
Only the two recorded losing surfaces are stopped and the winner remains readable until collection completes.
The repository is unchanged by all racers.
All agent processes, events, notifications, and owned Cmux resources reach terminal cleanup state.

cleanup: Collect the winner, stop every remaining provider, and close only resources in the ownership ledger.
Clear run-owned notifications where supported, remove the disposable repo, and compare the baseline tree.
